sections.overview: This noctuid moth is distributed across Europe and eastward to Siberia.
sections.identification: The British account gives a wingspan of 34–40 mm; this size overlaps with the related T. decimalis.
sections.habitat: It occurs in extensive grasslands, from dry nutrient-poor turf to wetland complexes and large woodland clearings.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on grasses, including mat-grass and wavy hair-grass in British records.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in August and September; young caterpillars climb grass stems at night to feed.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillar overwinters and remains active into early summer, while the adult flight is late summer.
sections.ecology: Compared with T. decimalis, its caterpillars stay green longer and mature about a month later; see that profile.
sections.conservation: The regional British source used here reports regular records at only one site in Hampshire; that local pattern is not a global assessment.
